why: (1) al2o3-pw's poly6 cells, which crashed on a band-solver bug now fixed: each scale on its own runner with four k-point workers. (2) How Bl₂Px₃'s plane-wave energies converge: the ionic model's two best cells at Γ, ecut 15–30, with the default and a softer pseudopotential set; the gap between them is what has to converge. (3) The same softening in ours, where PBE knows the answer: the four aluminas with soft Al and O at ecut 25 — does corundum's lead survive?
